title: The baby moved from St. Roch graveyard and Glass's garbage-wagon work
summary: Glass speaks of his baby Leona's grave and his job driving the city garbage wagon that filled in St. Roch Street.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And they got that little girl at the Cathedral Church. That's supposed to be my baby. At the Cathedral Church? At the Cathedral Church, a little black baby. It's in the Cathedral Church and they moved that from St. Rock Graveyard. Called Leona. Mama took and went to Fish Fry and come back home and give her the breast. And she died of poison. That was my little baby from St. Rock Graveyard. The fella showed me the baby. Though they moved it. He told me, he said they're going to move your baby. He used to work there. They called him English. See we all used to stay right there. I used to play in that St. Rock Graveyard. They didn't have no fence around. They used to be where we played. You see that St. Rock Street, we took and fixed that with garbage. I worked for every one of the ward leaders. When one would die, they didn't put me with that one. With the winners. You know, I'd drive every one of the ward leaders. When the husband died, I'd drive the city wagon. And I used to win the prize every year. We'd have to have inspections for them garbage cars. I didn't pick up nothing but paper and stuff. Oyster shells around the place. And we, that St. Rock Street is nothing but garbage. You filled it in with garbage? I filled it all the way from the market, all the way around to Franklin Avenue. That's all garbage. We'd cut many horses, mules, they'd fall on and bog up in it and they'd cut their, they'd have to kill them, you know. They'd have to come in and kill them. All that's garbage.
